title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-jordan-wip
content:
Context:
- Intermittent metrics drops observed starting 2026-02-18 02:30 UTC. Affected teams: hosted-api, dedicated-routing. Traces continue to ingest but metrics ingestion has gaps (prometheus remote_write targets show spike in 5xx).
- Related to recent otel-collector config change (PR #42) that introduced an extra filters/stats processor. Hypothesis: filter/processors path is dropping some metric families or causing backpressure to downstream forwarder.

What I saw (high-level):
- grafana: prometheus_remote_write_errors spiked from 0 -> ~220/min.
- metrics-aggregator queue length increased; pod restarts noted for metrics-forwarder in cluster obs-prod-1.
- logs show: "failed to send batch: 503 ServiceUnavailable upstream" from metrics-forwarder; curl to remote endpoint returns 200 but with slow responses (~1.2s).

Commands & snippets tried (timeline + output extracts):
1) Check otel-collector logs (metrics path)
$ kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=2h | grep -i metrics
2026-02-18T02:32:11Z ERROR metricsprocessor: failed to process metrics: dropped 12/68 "metric family not supported"
2026-02-18T02:35:02Z WARN  pipeline: send failed: upstream=metrics-forwarder code=503 

2) Check metrics-forwarder pod restarts and logs
$ kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=metrics-forwarder -o wide
metrics-forwarder-5fd7c    2/3     CrashLoopBackOff   6          3h
$ kubectl -n observability logs metrics-forwarder-5fd7c -c forwarder --tail=200
2026-02-18T02:33:00Z ERROR forwarder: failed to send batch to prometheus-remote (url=https://metrics-prod.company.internal/api/v1/write): 503 
2026-02-18T02:33:00Z ERROR forwarder: response body: "{"error":"upstream overloaded"}"

3) Trace check to ensure traces still flowing
$ kubectl -n observability logs deploy/trace-router -c trace-router --since=4h | grep 4acb1d
2026-02-18T02:32:10Z INFO span-received trace_id=4acb1d8aef2b0c7 span_id=1a2b3c
-> traces look OK for same timeframe (we have span samples)

4) Confirm remote endpoint health from a pod in same AZ
$ curl -kv https://metrics-prod.company.internal/api/v1/health -I
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: envoy
X-Envoy-Upstream-Service-Time: 1200ms

Observations: slow slow (1.1-1.4s) responses from remote.

5) Local repro: push a small batch from otel-collector debug endpoint
- Inserted a tiny metric family and watched otel-collector pipeline. No immediate drop. But when load increased (simulated with 50 concurrent pushes), observed 503 from forwarder and then otel logged dropped metrics.

Error snippets copied for context:
- "metricsprocessor: failed to process metrics: dropped 12/68 "metric family not supported""
- "failed to send batch to prometheus-remote (url=...): 503"
- "response body: {"error":"upstream overloaded"}"
- otel-collector WARN: "failed to enqueue batch: queue is full"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Upstream prometheus-remote endpoint is transiently overloaded and returning 503s under burst -> forwarder retries/backpressure cause queue growth -> otel drops metrics when internal queue full. (Likely)
2) New metrics processor filter (PR #42) mis-classifies some metric families, causing them to get dropped earlier in pipeline. Error text "metric family not supported" aligns with this. (Possible)
3) Network path: AZ-local egress/ENI issues causing slow responses from the remote endpoint. (Less likely; would expect other services to show same pattern)
4) Memory leak in metrics-forwarder causing restarts under load leading to temporary loss. (Check container memory OOMs)

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (done / pending):
- Done: confirmed 503s from forwarder logs and slow X-Envoy-Upstream-Service-Time header on health check to remote -> supports hypothesis 1.
- Done: otel-collector logs contain explicit "metric family not supported" lines -> supports hypothesis 2 for a subset of metrics. Need to correlate which families.
- Pending: check pod OOM and memory metrics for metrics-forwarder over the period (prometheus query to inspect container_memory_rss_bytes).
- Pending: run load test from another AZ to see if problem AZ-specific.

Debug steps taken and results:
- Rolled back PR #42 in staging; metrics flows restored in staging. (Staging repro matched: applying PR causes metrics drops under moderate load)
- Created a temporary rate limit on otel-collector -> reduced forwarder 503s but still observed drops when rate limit hits.
- Captured pcap between otel-collector and forwarder in staging -> saw TCP retransmits during high-load window.

Next actionable items (short term):
- [ ] Correlate which metric families are reported as "not supported" and map to services (use stackdriver/logs or add more verbose otel logging).
- [ ] Check memory and OOM events for metrics-forwarder pods (kubectl describe pod + metrics query).
- [ ] Engage infra (network) to check for AZ egress latency anomalies around 2026-02-18 02:30 UTC. Include packet loss summary.
- [ ] Add a temporary retry/backoff tweak in forwarder (lower max in-flight) to surface backpressure earlier instead of dropping silently.
- [ ] Consider a circuit-breaker in otel-collector pipeline for metrics-forwarder failures so we don't drop unrelated metrics families.

Notes / random breadcrumbs: 
- Found a Slack thread: slack:#observability ts:1677722000.000100 where infra mentioned a maintenance window at 2026-02-18 02:00 UTC for a specific load-balancer. Need to confirm correlates with our timeframe.
- PR #42 changeset: added stats-processor that drops empty-series and rewrites some label sets. Suspect label rewrite produced an unsupported metric type for remote.
- Example trace id to follow in logs: 4acb1d8aef2b0c7 (span sample present but metrics for same request missing)

Longer-term thoughts:
- We should have end-to-end integration tests for collector->forwarder->remote under load that exercise new processors. Staging caught this, but it was quiet in staging until load increased. Need better load shaping.
- Improve visibility: emit a metric for "dropped_metric_families_total" from otel-collector when a processor drops families so we can alert.

If anyone picks this up: start with correlating the "metric family not supported" messages to actual metric names and timestamp in logs. I left temporary verbose logging enabled on a single otel-collector instance (otel-collector-debug-1) in staging for 48h; use that to grep the full metric names.

Attachments / artifacts to check:
- otel config (PR #42) -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-config/pull/42
- metrics-forwarder logs: kubernetes pod metrics-forwarder-5fd7c (logs archived to s3://redwood-obs-archives/2026-02-18/metrics-forwarder-5fd7c.log)
